title: OpenAI to Train India's Civil Servants in AI via iGOT Karmayogi
description: OpenAI and Karmayogi Bharat signed an MoU to bring AI courses to the iGOT Karmayogi platform, reaching over 1.7 crore government employees across India.
tldr: Karmayogi Bharat and OpenAI signed an MoU on 21 October 2026 to bring AI learning to India's civil services.
Approved OpenAI Academy content will be added to the iGOT Karmayogi platform for government staff across the Centre and states.
More than 1.7 crore government employees are already registered on iGOT Karmayogi.
The move pushes practical AI skills into government, not just the private sector.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: On Wednesday, 21 October 2026, Karmayogi Bharat and OpenAI announced a memorandum of understanding aimed at strengthening AI capacity across India's civil services. Karmayogi Bharat is the government-owned not-for-profit company that runs iGOT Karmayogi, the learning platform used by government officials. The partnership is meant to help personnel engage with artificial intelligence confidently and responsibly, and to turn those new skills into better public outcomes, according to the joint release reported by PTI.

As part of the agreement, OpenAI will provide approved OpenAI Academy content to iGOT Karmayogi, while Karmayogi Bharat will handle access, learner engagement and coordination with the relevant government departments. The stated goal is to keep capacity building in step with the changing needs of government and to support Mission Karmayogi's vision of a future-ready civil service.

sections.heading: Who does what
paragraphs: Karmayogi Bharat operates and manages the iGOT Karmayogi platform, which is built to offer learning at any time, on any device, so that officials can improve their competencies without stepping away from their duties. Under this collaboration, OpenAI's capacity-building resources will be folded into that existing learning ecosystem for government personnel across both the Centre and the states.

Chhavi Bhardwaj, chief executive of Karmayogi Bharat, said that as technology reshapes governance, civil servants need practical skills they can apply directly in their day-to-day work, and that bringing OpenAI Academy resources to the platform should help personnel use AI confidently and responsibly. Pragya Misra, head of strategy and government affairs at OpenAI India, said India's AI opportunity will depend not only on access to technology but on how effectively people and institutions use it.

sections.heading: The scale behind the plan
paragraphs: The platform already reaches a very large audience. More than 1.7 crore government employees across the Centre, states and Union Territories are registered on iGOT Karmayogi, which makes it one of the largest workplace learning systems in the country. It hosts thousands of courses, including a growing set on artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, alongside functional and behavioural modules. That catalogue has grown steadily, and the AI and emerging technology modules are meant to help officials keep pace with tools that are changing how documents, data and citizen queries are handled.

Mission Karmayogi itself was launched in September 2020, with the aim of moving the civil services from a rules-based approach to a roles-based one and building a more citizen-centric administration. Central government employees and officers of the All India Services are expected to complete prescribed courses each year, and that progress is captured in their annual performance appraisal reports.

sections.heading: Why it matters for Indian readers
paragraphs: For students and young professionals, the signal is that AI literacy is no longer only a private-sector concern. When the machinery of government starts training its own staff at this scale, the baseline expectation shifts: knowing how to use AI tools well, and knowing when not to trust their output, becomes a core workplace skill rather than a specialist one. That can influence what colleges teach, what employers screen for, and how quickly everyday services move online.

For small businesses and ordinary citizens, an AI-literate administration can translate into faster file movement, clearer guidance and better service delivery at the counter. The partnership is also a reminder of how India is approaching AI: pairing a push for homegrown and sovereign capability with tie-ups with global AI firms for skills and content. The two tracks are running at the same time, and this deal sits on the skills side. For a country that is building its own AI models and data centres at the same time, the skills layer is easy to overlook, yet it decides whether the technology actually gets used well on the ground.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The announcement sets out intent rather than a full rollout plan. The details that will decide how much of this reaches the ground, such as which courses are offered first, how they are made available in Indian languages, and how learning is measured, are not spelled out in the release. The test will be whether the training is genuinely used in daily work and not just completed for the record.

Two questions are worth tracking. First, will the content suit the realities of officials working in districts far from big cities, where connectivity and time are both limited. Second, how will responsible use be built in, given that AI tools can be confidently wrong. The release stresses responsible use and better public outcomes, but the proof will come from how the courses are designed and adopted over the coming months.

faq.a: iGOT Karmayogi is the government's learning platform for civil servants, run by the company Karmayogi Bharat. It offers online courses that officials can take at any time and on any device.

faq.q: Who can use the OpenAI Academy courses on the platform?
faq.a: The courses are meant for eligible government personnel across the Centre, states and Union Territories. The release says access and learner engagement will be managed by Karmayogi Bharat with the relevant departments.

faq.q: Why train civil servants in AI?
faq.a: The stated aim is to help officials use AI confidently and responsibly in their day-to-day work, so that new capabilities lead to better public service delivery and outcomes for citizens.
